wired_receiver.readiness_rule: 64 recent detected transitions, each with absolute loop error below 0.1 UI; edge history clears after more than 64 transition-free observations. Assigned model rule, not a protocol tolerance mask.
assumptions: Existing four-observation feedback receiver with its assigned 5 ps IID detector timestamp noise.
Fixed physical two-pole channel, 400 mV nominal differential peak with optional declared amplitude scale, zero voltage decision threshold.
Random NRZ fixture; independent held-out scoreboard interval; no source labels reach the controller.

Sinusoidal or supplied multi-tone aperture displacement moves all analog observations; voltage noise plus DC offset precedes decisions. Supplied tones must guarantee monotonic time. Assigned stresses, not measured spectra.
unresolved: Detector timestamp noise is not transmitter or sampling-clock jitter.
Zero decision errors do not establish the 100 mV envelope threshold, BER or protocol compliance.

Optional rail-proportional gain is an assigned sensitivity. Driver placement propagates continuous forcing through channel/CTLE state; receiver placement scales the observed signal. Neither is a measured device law.
Optional CTLE is a stable unity-DC lead transfer before the assigned output noise/offset; its gain bandwidth, added noise, internal swing and current still require circuit evidence.
Physical detector, stochastic noise tails, SSC, longer runs and voltage/timing variation remain open.

receiver.scope: Shared loaded source/input/supply spectrum and 236 mA mode budget. Assigned instantaneous early-gain rail sensitivity; fixed NF/IIP3 and ideal linear filter internals. Input acquisition uses linear endpoints; half-LSB midpoint convention is assigned. The fixed comparator interval is an allocation, not demonstrated metastability performance.

load_response.scope: Local reference recharge port only, superposed with host ripple at full planning DC. Positive source charge is conserved; sink current receives no supply-energy credit. Assigned 200 ps supply-current pole requires an internal charge path; not a validated buffer. FFT guards, finite grid and linear fixed PDN do not qualify physical peak current or broadband transistor noise.

converter_precision.scope: Known sine characterization, not protocol training. I and Q are tested together against their shared reference. Full-scale-normalized ENOB includes residual harmonic distortion and noise after fitting only a fundamental and DC. This stimulus has its own reference-current/PDN feedback; it does not borrow an OFDM load trajectory. Assigned noise, poles, midpoint-held supply sensitivity and comparator interval still need physical evidence.

converter_reference_feedback.scope: Closed behavioral reference-load feedback under assigned device dynamics. Slower poles are uncertainty probes, not measured process corners. This supplements rather than relabels the retained assigned-ENOB RF/packet cases.

limitations: Source amplitude, receiver noise, threshold offset and AM depth are explicit hypotheses, not a qualified input circuit.
Two declared downstream noise allocations; stationary white-equivalent noise in 1 kHz–8 MHz.
Input AM at 1 MHz; cyclostationary additive-noise modulation omitted.
Source PM passes with unity gain; loaded sideband dispersion, stage power/startup and supply correlation unqualified.
Absolute static propagation delay omitted; no latency or input-circuit qualification.
input_noise_reference.source_peak_interpretation: Gain-equivalent ideal-ground parameter only; physical amplitude is physical_source_peak_v.

load.scope: Negative incremental driver current returns to its already-budgeted 28 mA; no extra DC load. Coupled tied-return PDN and REF_IN source impedance are retained. Guarded periodic FFT approximation with settled endpoint checks; input voltage requires threshold-event solving. Grid and guard controls remain necessary, not physical wake or bias-readiness qualification.

electrical.scope: Conservative declared port voltage/current/energy bounds; no physical parameter validation, clipping waveform, noise or matching-network qualification

coupled_load_clock.scope: Unique ordered local root continuations; extra crossings outside the brackets are not independently excluded.

transmitter.scope: Selected native 10-bit DAC and third-order reconstruction at the existing 20 MHz wideband cutoff. Same shared rail/reference/clock realization as RX, external observer with ideal framing and known DATA training. Broad power bands are not a spectral mask. A supplied driver-wake trajectory changes rail/reference/timing and available tail-current limit within the existing 28 mA reservation; otherwise warm constant bias. No signal-dependent RF-cycle current, physical DAC glitches, real FIFO/control lifecycle or external RF filtering. Output impedance/distortion and ENOB remain assigned requirements.

Word consumption uses corrected shared-environment TX edges; forwarded pacing counts the same clock divided by eight with assigned two-word observation delay. Only the first 2600 emitted bits feed the peer window; transport identity extends over the full run. Startup ready and prefill are assumed; reference halt tests logical underflow, not physical pad muting/recovery. Complete storage inventory, physical CDC, supply-dependent logic delay and driver-current feedback remain open.

Only a short emitted window feeds the independent peer; 1200 held-out bits per phase/ppm corner are not BER qualification. No shared-clock cancellation. clock.reason: Incomplete/unordered/unresolved edges or outside the assigned incremental input-voltage bound; no repaired clock substituted.

source_swing_controls.scope: 2.5 Gb/s NRZ source boundaries use corrected loaded REF_IN timing, assigned source/input noise and correlated supply delay. Rail-proportional NRZ drive propagates through persistent driver/load/CTLE state using exact sinusoidal forcing between actual bit edges; it is not multiplied onto the channel output. The assigned drive/rail law still needs device evidence. Direct-source controls are supplemented by finite host transport and eight nominal word-launch phases at the current package target. Only a short emitted window feeds the independent peer; 1200 held-out bits per phase/ppm corner are not BER qualification. No shared-clock cancellation. Internal serializer setup/hold, continuous/asynchronous host phase, driver-current feedback, pad nonlinearities, cable loss and protocol compliance remain open.

wired_transmit.scope: 2.5 Gb/s NRZ source boundaries use corrected loaded REF_IN timing, assigned source/input noise and correlated supply delay. Rail-proportional NRZ drive propagates through persistent driver/load/CTLE state using exact sinusoidal forcing between actual bit edges; it is not multiplied onto the channel output. The assigned drive/rail law still needs device evidence. Direct-source controls are supplemented by finite host transport and eight nominal word-launch phases at the current package target. Only a short emitted window feeds the independent peer; 1200 held-out bits per phase/ppm corner are not BER qualification. No shared-clock cancellation. usb_static_voltage.source: USB 2.0 section 7.1.1 and Table 7-7: high >=2.8 V into 15 kohm; low <=0.3 V with 1.5 kohm to 3.6 V. https://www.seriesten.org/docs/protocols/USB_2.0_Specification.pdf
usb_static_voltage.scope: Full 96 mA wired allocation versus 48 mA active bidirectional branch plus 2 mA inactive other branch, within existing owners. CORE/HOST/timing remain fully reserved, with the same worst-rate host harmonics. Die-return motion is included in board-referenced pad voltage. Nominal-source AC spectra retained at DC source corners. Static affine driver/capacitance and resistive compliance loads only; no signal-bond inductance, cable, edge-rate control, switching injection, pad-current PDN feedback, voltage-dependent drive or complete USB lifecycle.

usb_hs_levels.source: USB-IF USB 2.0 Electrical Compliance Test Specification v1.07 EL_9 and section 4.3: undriven high-speed pin voltage with precision 45-ohm loads. https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/USB%202%200%20Electrical%20Compliance%20Specification(v1.07).pdf
usb_hs_levels.rate_control_scope: Counterfactual simultaneous D2H/H2D slowdown, unchanged host transition charges, pulse shapes, total current reservation and package. Recompute internal-current location and harmonic frequencies, retaining at least the original absolute frequency coverage (1.875 GHz D2H, 937.5 MHz H2D); control follows H2D physical clock /4. Eight- and 64-word frame calculations include only the existing H2D CDC budget; D2H CDC, cable and physical timing margins remain missing, so a passing number cannot qualify turnaround. Slower rates are not adopted architecture settings.
usb_hs_levels.scope: Both host and device use the same local electrical branch. Released/J/K static conditions at worst-rate host activity, full single-branch current reservation, board-referenced peer loads, local inactive capacitance and signal bonds. Termination return current closes into the common PDN at every host harmonic. DC and unfiltered instantaneous +/-20 mV guards are reported separately, with explicitly hypothetical single-pole observer bandwidth controls; none establishes the correct compliance instrument response. Asymmetry values are sensitivity probes, not process tolerances. No transmission line, current-source output impedance/noise/supply dependence, switched drive, transient readiness, real comparator or FPGA negotiation lifecycle.

return_partition.scope: Five-node linear routing requirements at unchanged host rate, edge charge, 242 mA wired / 236 mA RF budgets and 500 pF reservoir. Hypothetical existing ground groups, not a provider bond assignment. Matching tied-return control preserves original parallel return R/L. The 0.2 host share is an equal-per-site impedance hypothesis for the two north/south ground sites versus eight east/west sites, not extracted conductance or an approved isolated ring. Quiet pad terminations close into the wired network and are disabled in RF mode; host return can still enter the quiet reservoir through shared supplies. Moved input supply is a physical routing requirement, not relabeled current. Host reservoir allocation consumes existing capacitance, scaling ESR inversely with area. No mutual inductance, nonlinear substrate/ESD coupling, physical GPIO capture, RF packet/clock qualification or fabrication proof. RF comparisons propagate quiet rail to voltage, reference and supply-induced phase at fixed 54 dB gain, retaining the same external source/input noise. They use assigned-ENOB conversion; causal SAR load feedback and other benches still require the partitioned network before any architecture adoption. The external REF_IN response to moving quiet ground and its own return current are not yet included; source/input noise remains assigned. Ground differences and both rail envelopes are retained; a quiet pin alone cannot select a mitigation.

reference_return.scope: Coupled passive single-ended REF_IN: 0.5 V peak Thevenin source, 50.2 ohms, 2 nH signal bond, 3 pF input, 20 mV incremental threshold. Both source carrier return and host-induced local input voltage are solved in the same PDN. Assigned 0.1 ps/mV, 1 GHz-pole downstream supply delay is evaluated at the actual input crossings, including the returned carrier; combined timing retains correlation rather than adding RMS values. Wired full-duplex 288 mA and RF 236 mA reservations retained; no USB test terminations are active. One coherent nominal-rate period, rising edges resolved at 32 and 64 samples/UI with bracketed roots. Source-only controls remove host tones without changing loading. No receiver bias/common-mode or protection model, source AM/noise, additive receiver noise, qualified threshold/supply sensitivity, autonomous PLL, fractional host-rate/phase corners or RF/serial payload propagation. Existing full-chip payload benches still omit this direct input-ground path; their clock results remain conditional until migrated.

reference_payload.scope: Corrected deterministic REF_IN edges and correlated supply delay now drive RF LO phase and ADC/DAC event timing. Both supply-sensitivity signs are tested. A same-grid previous-environment control separates migration from a mere envelope-sampling change; it is not a single-impairment intervention. Same coupled network drives rail/headroom and reference modulation, including returned source carrier. The baseline covers every package; split hypotheses are compared at the current package target. Source/AM/input phase allocations are retained and gain-normalized to loaded carrier amplitude as small perturbations, not solved jointly at the analog threshold. Rising-edge interpolation does not qualify duty cycle, quadrature or regenerated waveform harmonics; Noiseless 256/512 envelope-grid controls, plus 1024 at 2.4 GHz, test numerical sensitivity; the 2.4 GHz RX EVM is not yet converged. Invalid edge records are rejected before payload simulation. Main sweep uses assigned-ENOB ADC/DAC and known DATA training. Tied positive-sensitivity 2.484 GHz cases additionally close causal SAR recharge through loaded REF_IN and threshold events at moderate wanted power. Tied-return weak-signal causal feedback covers both RF endpoints and sensitivity signs. Driver wake and wired consumers have separate joined campaigns; real wideband preamble/packets and physical devices remain unqualified.

wideband_diagnosis.scope: Same weak wanted signal, blocker, waveform/noise seeds, package and mode budget. One-effect interventions identify causal requirements; disabled noise, altered clock-input requirements and higher assigned ENOB are diagnostic, not free circuit upgrades. Gains remain a fixed sweep, not oracle AGC. Known DATA training, finite phase lines and uncoded BPSK errors do not establish Wi-Fi packet sensitivity or compliance.

assumptions: The same linear common feed/branch/return model as retained studies, not measured assembly impedance.
H2D internal charge is part of the 110 mA HOST allowance, routed locally. No second timing C*V*f load is added.
Reserve current is a constant load; converter, core, inactive detection and output load-change spectra still need explicit bounds.
Higher-inductance case is an uncertainty probe, not an asserted process/package maximum.
Timing uses the retained external source, high-impedance input and assigned supply-to-delay transfer; no autonomous PLL or GF180 qualification.
missing_for_complete_baseline: physical SAR/reference poles, comparator regeneration, mismatch and full load/noise qualification; conditional closed-loop conversion/reference-load feedback is now modeled
calibrated narrowband air-boundary turnaround and broader packet coverage; wideband still uses known DATA training and ideal boundaries
actual RF noise/linearity and transition-dependent current with these loaded rails

corrected REF_IN timing joins wideband RF and a moderate-signal tied-return SAR feedback control; weak-wideband causal SAR and bounded driver-wake now use corrected input and supply feedback; real packet acquisition, stage-specific sensitivities and transient edge completeness remain open; wired recovery now uses corrected shared rails with independent CDR, and wired_transmit propagates nonuniform TX edges through the channel with independent peer CDR; serializer logic and driver-current feedback remain open; corrected narrowband packets retain failures
generic wired RX recovery is joined; protocol-specific pad/driver, electrical startup and full duplex lifecycle remain open
host current distribution per physical bond, GPIO timing and complete 8192-bit storage ceiling
supply-dependent AC spectra, thermal feasibility and stage-specific device variation
coverage_scope: Every existing joined bench runs each catalog entry. This does not supply missing full-chip behaviors or protocol qualification.

current_target_observations.scope: Selected package target and original 0.5 V source only. Numerical convergence is separate from signal acceptance. Mitigation controls do not replace baseline failures; these are fixture observations, not protocol verdicts or chip-completeness scores.

nominal_launch_phases.scope: Eight nominal word-launch phases times four peer corners; not an asynchronous phase bound or a chip-completeness count.
